title: Grammar Edit — Sentence Repair
description: Choose the edit that makes each sentence clear and grammatically correct.
subject: rla

questions.prompt: The manager, along with the two new hires, {{blank}} attending the safety training on Monday.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'manager,' which is singular. The phrase 'along with the two new hires' does not change the subject, so 'is' is correct.
questions.rule: Find the true subject first. Ignore extra phrases between the subject and the verb.

options.whyWrong: The nearby phrase mentions two hires, but the true subject is the singular noun 'manager.'
This changes the sentence to past tense when the sentence is written in the present.
This plural verb phrase does not match the singular subject 'manager.'

questions.prompt: The two engineers reviewed {{blank}} notes before the meeting.
questions.explanation: 'Their' shows that the notes belong to the two engineers and fits directly before the noun 'notes.'
questions.rule: Before a noun, check which word has the exact grammatical job the sentence needs.

options.whyWrong: 'There' refers to a place. The sentence needs a word that shows the notes belong to the engineers.
'They're' means 'they are,' which does not fit before the noun 'notes.'
'Theirs' can stand alone, but the sentence needs a possessive word directly before 'notes.'

curriculum.learningObjective: Choose the verb or word form that makes a sentence grammatically correct and clear.
